findings.title: Storage create and update failures record legacy metrics instead of storage metrics
findings.body: In `DualWriterMode3.Create` (line 45) and `DualWriterMode3.Update` (line 129), when `d.Storage.Create` or `d.Storage.Update` returns an error, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`. Conversely, in `DualWriterMode3.DeleteCollection` (line 166), the asynchronous `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` call records its duration via `d.recordStorageDuration` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`. This misattributes storage failures to legacy metrics and legacy delete-collection metrics to unified storage.

findings.title: Delete passes resource name instead of kind to metric label causing high cardinality
findings.body: In `DualWriterMode3.Delete` at line 106, `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes `name` (the individual resource's name/UID) as the `kind` argument, whereas every other metric call passes `options.Kind`. Additionally, at line 97, `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` is called instead of `klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`, dropping the `name`, `kind`, and `method` log values created on line 96. Passing `name` into a Prometheus metric label meant for `kind` will cause unbounded label cardinality as unique resource names are deleted.

findings.title: Asynchronous legacy writes use request context that is canceled when the HTTP handler returns
findings.body: In `Create` (line 51), `Delete` (line 110), `Update` (line 135), and `DeleteCollection` (line 163), the background goroutine derives its timeout context from the request `ctx` (`context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`). Because the outer method returns immediately after the unified storage operation finishes, the HTTP server will cancel the request `ctx` as soon as the response is sent, aborting the in-flight asynchronous legacy write before it can complete (unless `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` is used).

findings.title: Asynchronous Legacy.Create races with generated names and mutates shared object
findings.body: In `DualWriterMode3.Create` (line 55), the background goroutine passes the original `obj` (rather than `created` or a deep copy of `created`) to `d.Legacy.Create(ctx, obj, ...)`. First, if the object used `generateName` (as tested in `playlist_test.go` with `playlist-generate.yaml`), `d.Storage.Create` populates the generated name on `created`, while `obj` may not have it or `Legacy.Create` will generate a different UID/name in the legacy store, causing the two stores to diverge. Second, because the caller receives `created` (which may share underlying state with `obj`) and continues processing it on the request goroutine while `Legacy.Create` reads/mutates `obj` concurrently, this introduces a data race.

findings.title: Unit tests share a single testify Mock across concurrent goroutines without synchronizing
findings.body: In `dualwriter_mode3_test.go` (`TestMode3_Create`, `TestMode3_Delete`, `TestMode3_DeleteCollection`, `TestMode3_Update`), both `legacyStoreMock` and `storageMock` wrap the same `m := &mock.Mock{}` instance, and the tests return immediately after `dw.<Method>` returns while the background goroutine is concurrently calling methods on `ls` (which records calls into `m.Calls`). Furthermore, in the error test cases (e.g. `TestMode3_Create` line 40), `setupLegacyFn` registers the error expectation on `m`, which is actually consumed by `us.Create` only because both mocks share `m`. Sharing a `mock.Mock` across goroutines without waiting for the async goroutine to finish causes data races under `go test -race` and does not verify that `Legacy` was actually called.
